title: Right to Read Week VIP Visits
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
AHOY 

MARSHALL 

FAMILIES 

⚓📚

AHOY MARSHALL FAMILIES ⚓📚

We are excited to announce that March 23–27, 2026, we will be celebrating Right to Read Week with a fun, pirate-themed adventure: BOOKaneers: Finding Treasure in Books! Reading opens the door to imagination, discovery, and lifelong learning—and we can’t wait to celebrate the treasure found inside books with our students all week long.As part of our celebration, students will have the opportunity to invite a VIP (Very Important Pirate) to join them during their scheduled library time. VIPs may be parents, grandparents, special family members, or other important adults in your child’s life.During this special visit, VIPs and students will:Read together (bring a favorite book from home or choose one from our library collection)Complete a fun directed drawing activityPlay a gameWe kindly ask all VIPs to sign up using this link so we can plan accordingly. (If you have more than one student, please fill one out for each student.) Additionally, any grown-up who would like to attend must have a completed volunteer application on file prior to coming in. The form can be emailed directly to Mrs. Jones or returned to your child’s teacher. If you have already completed a volunteer application and have one on file with the school, you are all set—no need to complete another one. On the day of your visit, please arrive 5–10 minutes before your child’s scheduled library time. VIP’s will need to bring an ID and sign in at the office. A staff member will greet VIPs and walk the group up to the library when it is time for the class to begin.

We look forward to welcoming our VIPs aboard for this exciting week of literacy fun!If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Mrs. Jones @ joness@talawanda.org or 513-273-3600.Stephanie JonesPrincipal

summary: Marshall Elementary will celebrate **Right to Read Week: BOOKaneers** from **March 23–27, 2026** with a pirate theme. Students may invite a VIP (parent, grandparent, or special adult) to join them during their scheduled library time to read together, complete activities, and play games. VIPs must [sign up online](link required), have a completed volunteer application on file with Mrs. Jones, bring ID, and arrive 5–10 minutes early to sign in at the office. **Library times by day:** Monday (Gronas 10:25-11:10, Mesler 11:20-12:05, Brock 12:55-1:40), Tuesday (Ziegler 9:30-10:15, Beaton 10:25-11:10, Lykins 11:20-12:05, Schaefer 1:50-2:35, Smith 2:45-3:30), Wednesday (Paluch 9:30-10:15, Toerner 11:20-12:05, Slattery 12:55-1:40, Mohler 1:50-2:35, Chasteen 2:45-3:30), Thursday (Kraushar 9:30-10:15, Birkemeier 10:25-11:10, Whitaker 1:50-2:35, Sparks 2:45-3:30).

Contact your student's Reading Corner teacher with questions.

title: February Reading Corner: Understanding Decoding Skills
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
TITLE 

TALK 

READING 

CORNER

TITLE TALK READING CORNER

February Newsletter
What does decoding mean?A simple definition for decoding is recognizing letter sounds or patterns and blending them together to translate a written word into speech. Decoding is a foundational reading skill (phonics) that must be developed to begin successful reading with fluency. This process begins with students recognizing their letters and sounds then blending the sounds to speak the word, i.e., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes cat.Here is an example of what happens when a student decodes a word:Recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh)Knowing the sounds they makeBlending those sounds together to read a wordActivities: Reading Rockets is a reputable research-based website for all things reading; and below are age-specific resources for decoding activities.Kindergarten:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activitiesFirst Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesSecond Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesThird Grade:Here is a video showing how a 3rd grade student uses syllables to decode longer words more easily.

summary: **Decoding** is the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and patterns and blending them together to read words aloud. The process involves recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh), knowing their sounds, and blending those sounds to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes "cat"). Grade-specific decoding activities and resources are available from Reading Rockets for [Kindergarten](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101), [First Grade](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities), [Second Grade](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities), and Third Grade (video showing syllable strategies for longer words).
